author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Voters in Canada's oil-rich province of Alberta are taking part in a historic referendum that could pave the way for a formal process towards independence. 
Supporters of separation argue that Alberta's vast energy resources subsidise other parts of Canada while federal policies restrict the province's economic potential. 
Opponents warn that the movement threatens national unity and accuse US Republican-linked political figures of helping amplify separatist campaigns. 
Prime Minister Mark Carney has urged Albertans to vote against separation, warning that Canada's future is at stake. 
More than one million people have already cast ballots in advance voting, while recent opinion polls suggest nearly 70 percent of Albertans favour remaining in Canada. 
However, campaigners on both sides say voter turnout could determine the outcome. 
The referendum would initiate a process towards a second, binding vote rather than immediately grant Alberta independence. 

Al Jazeera's David Mercer rep
title: Alberta independence referendum puts Canada's unity to the test

He issued an executive order waiving the restrictions and duties in the so-called Graham Act, saying it was in the national interests of the United States. The legislation, formulated by late Senator Lindsey Graham, sanctions banks, Kremlin officials and a shadow fleet of oil tankers.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and European leaders have condemned the deal. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said: “If we want to end this war, then we have to squeeze the aggressor.”

Trump is increasingly framing Zelenskyy as the stumbling block to peace. On October 10 he said it was “time for Ukraine to get a new president”. Their relationship hit a low point at the Oval Office in February 2025.

With the US midterms weeks away, Trump is under pressure at home over the war in Iran and soaring energy costs.
